title: Reputation without a Control Group
abstract: arXiv:2609.17617v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: An adviser who warns that a task is difficult may become harder to evaluate when her advice is followed more thoroughly. We study a long-lived adviser and successive short-lived workers who choose between standard and intensive implementation. Standard implementation reveals whether the warning was correct and gives the next worker an opportunity to acquire cost-saving practical knowledge. Intensive implementation protects the project but produces only occasional evidence about the adviser. We construct a stationary sequential equilibrium in which the adviser initially accepts an informative implementation, withholds the next project after her reputation improves, and resumes recommendations once inherited know-how has been lost. The interruption is chosen because it changes the successor's implementation decision: preserving know-how reverses the adviser's preference at the relevant history. translated_abstract: 当一个警告某项任务困难的顾问，其建议被越彻底地遵循时，她反而可能变得更难被评估。我们研究一个长期存续的顾问与相继接替的短期工人，他们在标准实施与强化实施之间进行选择。标准实施能够揭示警告是否正确，并让下一位工人有机会获得节省成本的实用知识；强化实施则保护了项目，但只能产生关于顾问的零星证据。我们构建了一个平稳序贯均衡：顾问最初接受信息性实施，在自身声誉改善后扣留下一个项目，并在继承的实用知识流失后重新恢复推荐。之所以选择中断，是因为它改变了继任者的实施决策：保留实用知识会在相关历史节点上逆转顾问的偏好。所有已实现的证据均保持公开。（注：原文摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文构建了一个平稳序贯均衡，证明长期顾问会在声誉改善后故意扣留项目、中断实用知识的积累，因为知识保留会促使继任者选择难以揭示其能力的强化实施，从而刻画了缺乏对照组环境下声誉激励导致建议中断的新机制。
en_tdlr: This paper constructs a stationary sequential equilibrium in which a long-lived adviser strategically withholds projects to interrupt successors' know-how accumulation once her reputation improves, because preserving know-how would lead successors to choose intensive implementation that makes her harder to evaluate.
